name: Jared Kushner

summary.text: Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law, served as senior adviser to the president in the first Trump administration (2017-21), with a portfolio that included Middle East policy, the January 2020 Israeli-Palestinian plan and the 2020 Abraham Accords normalisation agreements. After leaving office he founded the private equity firm Affinity Partners, whose capital came overwhelmingly from Gulf sovereign wealth funds, led by a $2 billion commitment from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. In the second Trump administration he took on an unpaid diplomatic role alongside envoy Steve Witkoff in Gaza negotiations, while congressional Democrats questioned the overlap between his diplomacy and his firm's Gulf investors.

facts.claim: As senior adviser to President Trump in the first term, Kushner was the driving force behind the administration's January 2020 Israeli-Palestinian plan and built relationships with Gulf partners while serving as a senior adviser on the Middle East; the Abraham Accords saw the UAE, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco normalise ties with Israel in late 2020 and early 2021.
facts.quote: He was the driving force behind Trump's first-term peace plan, which aimed to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and ultimately establish ties between Israel and Saudi Arabia.

sources.title: Jared Kushner reenters as key player in Middle East peace push
Jared Kushner on how Trump administration's unconventional approach led to historic Mideast peace deals

facts.claim: In May 2021, after leaving government, Kushner announced the Abraham Accords Institute for Peace, intended to deepen the agreements Israel reached with the UAE, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco.
facts.quote: In May 2021 he announced the Abraham Accords Institute for Peace, which aims to deepen the agreements Israel reached with the UAE, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco.

sources.title: Kushner Launches Group to Promote Arab States' New Ties With Israel

facts.claim: Kushner formed Affinity Partners shortly after leaving the White House in 2021; Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund committed $2 billion in June 2021 and the firm had raised about $3 billion by the end of that year. Kushner has said he did not plan to launch a private equity firm until after leaving the White House.
facts.quote: Kushner formed Affinity shortly after leaving the White House, and by the end of 2021 had raised $3 billion for a debut fund.

sources.title: Kushner's fund has reaped millions in fees, but so far returned no profits
Letter from Chairman Wyden to Lauren Key, Chief Financial Officer, A Fin Management LLC

facts.claim: A panel screening investments for the Saudi Public Investment Fund objected to the $2 billion commitment to Kushner's firm, citing management 'inexperience', an 'excessive' fee and 'public relations risks' tied to his White House role; the full PIF board, headed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, overruled it, according to New York Times reporting relayed by Middle East Eye and later described in Senate Finance Committee letters.
facts.quote: Despite the objections, the full board of the PIF - headed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, a close ally and beneficiary of Kushner's support when he worked at the White House - overruled the panel's objections.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia: Panel advising sovereign wealth fund objected to $2bn funding of Kushner firm
Letter from Chairman Wyden to Chad Mizelle, Chief Legal Officer, Affinity Partners

facts.claim: Senate Finance chairman Ron Wyden wrote in September 2024 that he viewed Affinity as 'likely part of a compensation scheme involving U.S. political figures designed to circumvent the Foreign Agents Registration Act', citing fees collected without capital being deployed in a timely fashion. This is a senator's allegation in a committee letter, not a finding.
facts.quote: Affinity's failure to deploy capital in a timely fashion while charging excessive fees has reinforced my view that Affinity is likely part of a compensation scheme involving U.S. political figures designed to circumvent the Foreign Agents Registration Act.

sources.title: Wyden Investigation of Kushner Firm Continues; New Letter Outlines Affinity Partners' Fee Structure, Lack of Return to Investors, Questionable Deals with Foreign Governments

facts.claim: Kushner said on the 'Invest Like The Best' podcast that talks on Affinity's additional $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and Lunate began in February 2024 and closed before the November 2024 U.S. election, and that the investors agreed to the extended commitments 'irrespective of the outcome' of the election.
facts.quote: He said that Affinity's investors agreed to the extended commitments "irrespective of the outcome", a reference to Trump's election.

sources.title: Kushner's Affinity raises new capital from QIA and Lunate

facts.claim: In the second Trump administration Kushner returned to a top role alongside special envoy Steve Witkoff in negotiations on a Gaza agreement; a White House spokeswoman said Kushner 'only acts in the best interests of the American public' when questions were raised about his firm's Gulf investors.
facts.quote: A White House spokeswoman said Kushner "only acts in the best interests of the American public."

sources.title: Jared Kushner Accused of Being 'Deeply Compromised' Over Millions in Fees From Countries With Which He Negotiates
Jared Kushner reenters as key player in Middle East peace push

facts.claim: Responding in October 2026 to a CNN report on Affinity's stake in the Israeli financial group Phoenix, Kushner said he has no role in deciding what Phoenix buys or sells and that Affinity does not own the defence companies highlighted; his attorney said any suggestion that his diplomatic work influenced Phoenix's investments, or vice versa, was incorrect.
facts.quote: He said he has no role in deciding what Phoenix buys or sells, and that Affinity does not own the defense companies highlighted in CNN's story.

sources.title: Jared Kushner scolds CNN over 'deeply misleading' report, says key info buried behind paywall
Jared Kushner's company has large stake in firm with Israeli military links

facts.claim: On March 19, 2026, House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia and Senator Ron Wyden wrote to the White House chief of staff about Kushner's fundraising from foreign governments while serving in a diplomatic role. The letter is a congressional request, not a finding.
facts.quote: Kushner has already increased the amount of fees he is collecting from foreign governments since his father-in-law took office in 2025.

sources.title: Letter from Ranking Member Garcia and Senator Wyden to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles

connections.claim: Kushner formed Affinity Partners in 2021 after leaving the White House and is the sole owner of its registered adviser, A Fin Management LLC, according to a regulatory filing.
connections.quote: The filing was made under the company name A Fin Management LLC, and the sole owner of the company is Jared Kushner.

openQuestions: Kushner's official White House biography (trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov) was not reached; his title and start date are recorded from secondary sources.

Kushner's written response to the New Yorker's 2025 investigation (reported to include 'I have never taken a diplomatic action to benefit Affinity') was not reached from a citable source and is omitted.
Whether Kushner's second-term role is formally unpaid or 'volunteering', as Affinity's chief legal officer described it, should be confirmed against an official record.
